text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police roll out tanks to check any demostrations on Thursday to mark the anniversary of the annulled June 12, 1993 presidential election.
- Jail sentences of three former executives of the liquidated Alpha Merchant Bank have been quashed by appeals tribunal which rules that failed banks tribunal exceeded its power by convicting them.
- Transport fares double in the capital Abuja as fuel scarcity bites harder.

- U.S. congressman Donald Payne introduces bill in his country's House of Representatives to bar American investment in Nigeria and to freeze Nigerian assets there over the African nation's slow pace of democracy and alleged human rights abuses.
- Nigerian foreign minister Tom Ikimi restates the resolve of West African force ECOMOG to reinstate the ousted elected president of Sierra Leone who was toppled by soldiers in a coup last month.
- The federal government has directed state oil firm NNPC to immediately make oil products available nationwide to end a persistent fuel shortage.

- Police have been drafted to protect the central Nigerian home of former military president retired General Ibrahim Babangida, whose government annulled the 1993 presidential poll, plunging the country into turmoil.
- Trade between Nigeria and Brazil doubled to more than half a billion dollars last year, according to figures released by the Brazilian embassy in Lagos.
